Of course you loose quite a bit intelligence that way, but if you use a local model (and for many actions a decision model), which can run on a lot of office workers hardware nowadays, you can just run everything locally: local model, local code interpreter sandbox, local file access.

If you don't send the data anywhere remotely (by using a local model, and restricting web access of the sandbox), you don't have to worry about exfiltration of sensitive contents of files, which heavily reduces the allowance prompts for the user.

Obviously that's not in the interest of OpenAI/Anthropic, who are the main providers of "general office work" desktop tools like Cowork.

The problem is that they loose some of the biggest utility that way. I want to be able to just say "draft a reply to email x". Because that is the lowest friction. I'm happy to read it back and sign-off. I don't have an answer as to how to do it securely, and am with you that the wanton disregard by big AI players for safety and security is demoralizing.

This goes to the biggest problem imho - that we've gone this far down the track of these agents being rolled out without proper sandboxing.

The agent should not be running on the same workstation. It should have a hard isolation barrier between it and the host machine. We shouldn't be starting from a fail-unsafe state and then trying to patch in security and isolation for these people. It should be deployed fail-safe and when they hit actual friction we can solve that.

Anthropic started out doing the right thing with Cowork (running in a VM). But it seems like they've ever since been walking that back and trying to get users to rely on automatic protections. I think it's just the wrong direction.
